title: Python SlotClaim.decode_cose accepts reordered payload keys and trailing payload bytes (deterministic-CBOR parity gap vs Rust/C)
description: Found during l2uk review (security pass, kimi-k3; verified against python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py). spec/decisions.jsonl slot-claim-cose-sign1 adjudicates the COSE payload as deterministic-CBOR. Rust from_cose now rejects non-ascending keys and trailing payload bytes (l2uk), and C rejects both implicitly (claim_compute_digest digests the received payload bytes, coap_slot_coord.c:394). Python decode_cose (slot_claim.py:198-233) uses cbor2.loads on the payload with no key-order check, no trailing-byte check, and no byte-equality re-encode gate; verify_slot_claim digests encode_claim_canonical(claim) (slot_claim.py:535), the canonical re-encode — exactly the pre-l2uk Rust behavior. Net: a relay can still flip Python vs {Rust,C} verdicts on a signature-valid claim with permuted keys or trailing payload bytes. Fix: in decode_cose, require payload keys strictly ascending (or byte-equality: encode_claim_canonical(decoded) == payload) and reject trailing payload bytes. Mitigating: l1qw.20 notes the Python wire receiver is currently missing, so live RF impact is deferred. Note: the l2uk bead description's claim of a Python '5rfl byte-equality gate' does not match the code — 5rfl closed bignum/long-form-uint leniency only.
close_reason: Landed the deterministic-CBOR payload gate on beads-worker-3 (commit 68b709d89a), adapting 5rfl's byte-equality gate (worker-5) to my strict-envelope-reader branch. decode_cose now builds the SlotClaim then requires encode_claim_canonical(claim) == payload, closing reordered keys, duplicate keys, unknown keys, trailing payload bytes, tag-2 bignums, and non-minimal long-form uints uniformly. Also applied main's ft5w type-strict mode check (type(mode) is not int) which my branch lacked. Tests: ported 5rfl's non-canonical-uint harness + added cb10-specific reordered/duplicate/unknown-key and trailing-byte cases, ft5w bool/float mode cases, and a canonical control that decodes AND verifies (True,None). 40 passed / 3 pre-existing skips. 3x codereview: correctness PASS (3 comment-accuracy findings, fixed in-diff), security PASS (2 P3 test-coverage findings, fixed in-diff), edge PASS (done directly after 2 reviewer timeouts; probes confirmed no false-positive, deterministic encode, ordinal=None unreachable at gate). Review findings filed as beads.
